about: the named ranges of radiation, in nanometres, short end first. the iso ones are iso 21348's, as its authors give them in their account of its draft: tobiska and nusinov, "status of iso draft international standard for determining solar irradiances (dis 21348)", cospar 2004, read 2026-10-31 from space environment technologies' copy (spacewx.com), section 3. each is as there: gamma 0.00001 to 0.001 nm, x-rays hard and soft together 0.001 to 10, extreme ultraviolet 10 to 120, ultraviolet 100 to 400, infrared 760 to 1 000 000, microwave 1 000 000 to 15 000 000 and radio 100 000 to 100 000 000 000, each from its short end up to but not including its long end. libtheme-css had typed extreme ultraviolet to 121, as its author recalled the published standard; the draft says 120, and the published iso 21348:2007 is not open and was not read, so it may differ. they overlap in places (ultraviolet and extreme ultraviolet; radio and microwave), and are carried as they came. fermi's is given in energies, 10 keV to 300 GeV, as nasa's heasarc gives the mission's range: "studies the cosmos in the energy range 10 keV – 300 GeV", read 2026-10-31 at heasarc.gsfc.nasa.gov/docs/heasarc/missions/fermi.html, where game run extract finds it. it is the mission's whole range as heasarc states it; its instruments each cover a part
